newsitem.title: UK: Tax costs forced rejection of LVMH plan-GrandMet.
newsitem.headline: Tax costs forced rejection of LVMH plan-GrandMet.

text.p: High tax costs, mainly in the United States, prompted British drinks giants' Grand Met and Guinness to reject a demerger proposal by French luxury goods company LVMH, Grandmet's chief executive John McGrath said on Friday.

Grandmet and Guinness on Friday jointly slammed LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault proposal to replace their 24 billion pound ($40.1 billion) two-way merger to one including LVMH. They said Arnault's plan would result in a value loss of at least 1.5 billion pounds.

Grandmet's McGrath told a telephone news conference that the one-off tax costs it would face while demerging its fast food chain Burger King and food processor Pillsbury from the planned linkup with Guinness would be too expensive for shareholders.

"The one off U.S. tax costs of separating the businesses, on the basis of estimated trading values for the relevant businesses would be of the order of 1.1 billion pounds," Grandmet said in a statement.
"Every investment bank has been at our door with proposals on how to get around that tax. Nobody has found a solution," McGrath said.
U.S. law forces a non-domicile business group to pay a one-off tax if it sells or spins off a subsidiary.

Arnault had proposed a demerger of Pillsbury, Burger King, Guinness Brewing and Drinksco into separate listed firms. He also wants to integrate LVMH's spirit division, Moet Hennessey with United Distillers and International Distillers & Vinters, divisions of Guinness and Grandmet respectively.
